reasoning_summary: 0001: Header, no mathematical content. 0002-0003: States the two-direction plan; legitimate. 0004: Definition of 2-connected as "connected with no cut vertices" is slightly incomplete (omits the order >= 3 / K2 caveat) but harmless here. 0005: Standard definition of plane graph; fine. 0006: Standard definition of face; fine. 0007: Informal definition of face boundary (edges/vertices incident to the face); acceptable. 0008-0009: Standard definition of bipartite; fine. 0010: Section header for the forward direction. 0011: Sets bipartition (A,B) and fixes an arbitrary face F; fine. 0012-0013: Asserts the boundary of every face of a 2-connected plane graph is a cycle. This is a true standard theorem (e.g. Diestel Prop. 4.2.6); the parenthetical is not a proof but citing the known result is acceptable. 0014: Names the boundary cycle C = v1...vk in cyclic order; fine given 0012. 0015: Along a cycle in a bipartite graph the classes alternate; correct. 0016: WLOG v1 in A, so vi alternates and vk is in B iff k even; correct bookkeeping. 0017: vk is adjacent to v1 in A, so vk in B, hence k even; correct. 0018: Concludes C is an even cycle; correct. Part 1 is sound. 0019: Section header for the converse. 0020-0021: Assumes every face boundary is an even cycle and announces a bipartition construction; fine as setup. 0022-0023: Invokes Whitney's ear decomposition for 2-connected graphs; true theorem, correctly stated. 0024-0025: Base case takes the (even) boundary cycle of some face and 2-colours it; valid, since an ear decomposition may start from any cycle. 0026-0027: Inductive setup (bipartite H with a proper 2-colouring, add ear P to get H'); fine as setup. 0028: FIRST FAILING STEP - asserts the two endpoints of the ear P "are colored, say, red and blue (since H is bipartite)". Bipartiteness of H gives no information about the relative colours of the two ear endpoints; they may well receive the SAME colour, and that is precisely the case in which the ear must be forced to have even length. The whole extension argument is built on this unjustified case assumption. 0029-0030: Compounds the error and is backwards under its own hypothesis: if the endpoints have different colours, an ODD-length ear extends consistently while an EVEN-length ear creates a monochromatic edge; the text claims the opposite. 0031: Asserts "the boundary of the new face created by adding P must be an even cycle". Unjustified: the region created inside the intermediate plane subgraph H' is a face of H', not a face of G, so the hypothesis (faces of G are even) does not apply to it; nothing guarantees an ear decomposition can be chosen so each ear closes off an actual face of G. 0032: Asserts the new face boundary is P plus a path in H; not established (the relevant portion of the boundary walk of the containing face of H' need not be a path, and this face is not a face of G anyway). 0033-0034: The parity-sum statement is correct only conditionally on the unjustified claims of 0031-0032, so it carries no force. 0035: "In a bipartite graph a path joining equally coloured vertices has even length, differently coloured odd length" is true. 0036-0037: Purely circular: it says the parity of P "must match appropriately" so the colouring extends, instead of deriving the parity of P from the hypothesis on faces of G; the key implication is asserted, not proved. 0038-0039: "Therefore we can always extend the 2-colouring along P" is unsupported, resting on 0028 and 0031. 0040: The inductive conclusion that G is properly 2-colourable inherits the gap and is therefore not established (the correct argument instead shows every cycle of a plane graph is a mod-2 sum of face boundaries, hence even). 0041-0043: Summary claiming both directions are proved; false for Part 2. 0044: Restatement of the theorem; not established by the given argument. 0045: Page number, no content. Verdict INVALID: Part 1 is correct, Part 2 fails first at line 0028 and again decisively at 0031.
